problem:
The position $s(t)$ of a particle (in meters) at time $t$ seconds is given by 

$$
s(t)=\sqrt{4{t}^{2}-7t+6},\,t\ge 0.
$$

Calculate the time at which the particle is stationary. Do not round your answer.

Therefore, the particle is stationary at $t=$
{{field-1}}
$\text{s}.$
worked_solution:
The particle is stationary when its velocity is zero. So first, we need to calculate the velocity function. We can do that by taking the derivative of the position function, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{4{t}^{2}-7t+6}) \\  & =\frac{8t-7}{2\sqrt{4{t}^{2}-7t+6}}\end{aligned}
$$

The particle is stationary when $v=0\,\text{m/s}.$ So, we set $v=0$ and solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8t-7}{2\sqrt{4{t}^{2}-7t+6}} & =0 \\ 8t-7 & =0 \\ t & =\frac{7}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the particle is stationary at $t=\frac{7}{8}\,\text{s}.$
